visual_events.label: Spreading and shaping mortar bed along brick-on-edge wall
visual_events.description: In a low-angle close/medium shot of a partially built red-brick wall laid on edge, the primary mason (on the left, wearing a beige shirt with a lavalier mic clipped to the placket) and an assistant (hands entering from screen left/right at 1.9s–3.8s) deposit and spread wet grey mortar along the top edges of the parallel brick courses. From 4.0s to 18.8s, the primary mason uses his pointed trowel to spread, level, and trim the mortar bed along the inner and outer wythes of the wall toward the foreground, while in the background an older worker in white walks toward the camera carrying an empty metal pan (exiting right around 7.5s) and another man stands observing on the far right.
visual_events.context_result: The top edges of the existing brick-on-edge course are covered with a fresh bed of wet mortar ready to receive the next course of bricks, leaving the internal cavities between bricks visible.
visual_events.camera_framing: Static low-angle tripod shot looking diagonally along the brick wall from foreground left toward background center.

visual_events.label: Layingfive successive bricks on edge along the outer face
visual_events.description: The primary mason sets down his trowel and lays five whole red bricks on edge sequentially along the outer (left) wythe of the wall, moving from mid-wall toward the camera foreground: Brick 1 is placed and aligned at 19.8s–23.3s; Brick 2 is placed and tapped into alignment with his hands at 24.8s–28.3s; Brick 3 is placed flush against the previous brick at 29.8s–32.5s; Brick 4 is placed and adjusted at 33.4s–35.7s; Brick 5 is placed in the near foreground at 36.6s–39.2s. He then places a sixth brick on the inner (right) wythe at 39.7s–42.4s, creating a parallel pair with a hollow cavity between them. In the background, the older worker in white re-enters at 37.5s carrying a pan of material on his shoulder toward the red building.
visual_events.context_result: Six bricks are positioned on edge in the new course, clearly demonstrating the vertical-edge orientation and the hollow cavity formed between parallel stretcher bricks.
visual_events.camera_framing: Static low-angle close/medium shot; mason's hands and forearms dominate the left foreground.

visual_events.label: Applying additional mortar and laying header/stretcher bricks in foreground
visual_events.description: At 43.6s–45.6s, the assistant's hand enters from screen right with a red-handled trowel to deposit and spread additional mortar on the foreground corner/inner wythe while the primary mason steadies the recently laid brick. At 48.6s–54.3s, the primary mason places a brick transversely (as a header bridging the wythes) in the foreground while the assistant deposits another trowel of mortar at 49.8s–51.8s. At 54.6s–59.8s, after brief mortar smoothing by the assistant, the primary mason places and aligns a foreground stretcher brick on edge along the outer face, with its yellowish-red end face prominent in the lower-left foreground.
visual_events.context_result: The foreground section of the rat-trap bond course is built up with both stretcher and header bricks on edge, enclosing rectangular internal cavities.
visual_events.camera_framing: Static low-angle shot; foreground bricks fill the lower left and center of the frame.

visual_events.label: Mason walking to far end of wall and checking vertical alignment with plumb bob
visual_events.description: While the assistant's trowel briefly touches mortar on the right at 63.8s, the primary mason walks away from the foreground along the left side of the wall toward the far corner (64.5s–66.0s), bends down to check the far end of the wall with a plumb bob (66.0s–67.3s), and walks back toward the foreground holding the plumb bob suspended from its string (67.3s–70.2s).

visual_events.uncertainty: Exact contact of the plumb bob against the far corner at 66s–67s is partially occluded by the mason's body and the wall.

additional_analysis.attempts: This 95.04-second clip is a single continuous camera recording from a fixed low-angle tripod position showing successive stages of building one course of a rat-trap bond brick wall (not repeated takes of the same brick). Within this continuous recording, there are distinct physical cycles and process stages that offer multiple editing options: Stage 1 (ve_01, 0.0s–18.8s, claim ce_01) shows mortar bed preparation, where an assistant helps deposit mortar at 0.0s–3.8s and the primary mason spreads and shapes the mortar bed along both wythes from 4.0s to 18.8s. Stage 2 (ve_02, 18.8s–43.2s, claims ce_02 and ce_03) comprises six successive brick-laying cycles where the mason places five outer stretcher bricks on edge (at 19.8s–23.3s, 24.8s–28.3s, 29.8s–32.5s, 33.4s–35.7s, and 36.6s–39.2s) and one inner stretcher brick on edge (at 39.7s–42.4s); each individual brick placement is a complete physical cycle, making ve_02 highly modular. Stage 3 (ve_03, 43.2s–63.0s, claim ce_04) shifts to the immediate foreground, where the assistant adds mortar with a red-handled trowel (43.6s–45.6s and 49.8s–51.8s) and the primary mason lays a transverse header brick (48.6s–54.3s) and a foreground stretcher brick on edge (54.6s–59.8s). Stage 4 (ve_04, 63.0s–71.0s, claim ce_05) shows the mason walking to the far corner of the wall to check plumb with a plumb bob and returning. Stage 5 (ve_05, 71.0s–83.0s, claim ce_06) includes placing a half-brick bat (71.4s–73.7s) followed by an on-site discussion and pointing gesture (74.7s–80.5s) before the mason steps back (80.5s–83.0s). Stage 6 (ve_06, 83.0s–95.04s, claim ce_07) shows two final foreground bricks being placed on edge (83.5s–88.1s and 89.6s–94.4s) to complete the foreground cavity box.

additional_analysis.continuity: Throughout all candidate segments (ve_01 through ve_06), the camera remains locked on a tripod in the exact same low-angle diagonal composition looking from the front-left corner of the wall toward the mid-ground right. Progressive material state changes on the wall must be respected if cutting multiple segments from this clip into the same sequence: in ve_01 (0.0s–18.8s, claim ce_01), the top course has only a fresh mortar bed and no bricks laid in the foreground half. In ve_02 (18.8s–43.2s, claims ce_02 and ce_03), six bricks are progressively added from mid-wall toward the foreground (five on the left outer face, one on the right inner face). In ve_03 (43.2s–63.0s, claim ce_04), a transverse header brick and a foreground outer stretcher brick (with a distinct yellowish-red end face) are added in the lower-left foreground. In ve_05 (71.0s–83.0s, claim ce_06), a half-brick bat is added behind the foreground header. In ve_06 (83.0s–95.04s, claim ce_07), two final bricks are added on the right/inner side of the immediate foreground. Therefore, any multi-cut condensation from this clip must stay in chronological order (e.g., mortar bed in ve_01 -> laying stretchers in ve_02 -> foreground header/stretcher in ve_03 -> closing cavity in ve_06) so bricks do not magically appear and disappear. Also note background continuity: the older worker in white (ent_bg_worker) walks toward the camera at 0.0s–7.5s, walks away carrying a pan on his head/shoulder at 37.5s–48.0s, and walks forward again at 56.0s–66.0s.
